title: Marketing spend
reading_md:
**What it measures.** What Voltmarkt paid for advertising media in a period: the cost of the clicks, views and placements bought on each channel.

**Formula.** Spend = SUM(daily spend) over the days in the period.

- Grain: channel or campaign × day or month.
- Month to date runs from the 1st of the month up to and including yesterday, the last complete day.

**Worked example.** September 2025:

| Channel | Spend |
|---|---|
| Paid search | €42,000 |
| Paid social | €28,000 |
| Display | €10,000 |
| Total | €80,000 |

An agency runs paid social and display for a 10% fee. Add the fee to both channels, giving €30,800 and €11,000, or to neither, and say which. Adding it to paid social only makes social look dearer than display for the same media.

**One source, one time zone.**

- Ad platforms report spend as the ads run. Finance books invoices, which can arrive later and include fees and credits, so the two totals rarely match. Pick one source for a report, use it for every channel, and name it.
- An ad platform exports days in the time zone its account is set to, which may be UTC. Voltmarkt reports in Amsterdam time, 1 hour ahead of UTC in winter and 2 in summer. Spend from 23:00 to midnight UTC on 30 November belongs to 1 December in Amsterdam. Convert every source to one time zone before you sum days into months.

**Common mistakes.**

- Mixing time zones.
- Mixing ad-platform and finance figures across channels.
- Including agency fees in one channel only.

**What it does not answer.**

- What the spend bought: that is cost per click, cost per acquisition or return on ad spend.
- Whether the spend was on plan: that is budget vs actual variance.

**How managers ask for it.** "How much did we spend on paid social in September?" "Give me spend by channel month to date."
